objectives.summary: A Security Copilot workspace is a tenant-bound container that sets where customer data is stored, which SCU capacity powers it, and who has access (owners and contributors are scoped per workspace). Organizations can create several workspaces to separate teams, regions or budgets. Capacity is measured in Security Compute Units (SCUs): provisioned SCUs are billed hourly, and optional overage SCUs absorb spikes. Microsoft 365 E5/E7 tenants can be auto-provisioned with a default workspace and capacity. Workspaces were introduced in public preview, while workspace-level plugin management is GA.

keyFacts.fact: A workspace defines the customer data storage location, the capacity that powers it, and who has access; owners/contributors are scoped per workspace.
Creating a workspace requires at least Security Administrator; attaching capacity also requires Azure subscription Owner or Contributor.
A workspace's data storage location is chosen at creation and can't be changed afterward.
Provisioned capacity requires a minimum of one SCU, refreshes each clock hour, and unused SCUs don't roll over; overage SCUs are billed on use (to one decimal) and can be capped or unlimited.
Owner settings apply per workspace, except audit logging enablement, which only Security Admins can change and which applies to all workspaces.

For eligible Microsoft 365 E5/E7 tenants, Security Copilot auto-creates a default virtual capacity and default workspace; embedded experiences in Defender, Entra, Purview and Intune use the default workspace.
Security Copilot workspaces were introduced in public preview; managing plugins at workspace level is generally available. Check the current status before your exam.

objectives.portalPath: Security Copilot portal (securitycopilot.microsoft.com) > workspace selector > New workspace; Home menu > Owner settings > Manage workspaces

lab.title: Create a second workspace with its own capacity
steps: Sign in to https://securitycopilot.microsoft.com as a Security Administrator who is also Contributor on an Azure subscription.
Open the workspace selector on the landing page and select New workspace.

Name it WS-Contoso-EU, create a new capacity (subscription, resource group, capacity name, prompt evaluation location, 1 SCU, overage limit), select the data storage location and data sharing preferences.
Accept the terms and select Create; then open Owner settings > Manage workspaces and confirm the capacity assignment.
Delete the capacity when finished to stop hourly billing (Owner settings > units > Change > ... > Delete the capacity).
lab.verify: WS-Contoso-EU appears in the workspace selector and in Manage workspaces with its capacity; Usage monitoring shows the capacity.

options: 3 provisioned SCUs only; requests above 3 are blocked

objectives.summary: Security Copilot has two platform roles, Copilot owner and Copilot contributor, which control platform features but grant no security data by themselves. Certain Entra and Purview roles (for example Global Administrator and Security Administrator) automatically inherit owner. Access to data still depends on each plugin's own RBAC, because Copilot uses on-behalf-of authentication. Best practice is to replace broad 'Everyone' contributor access with the Recommended Microsoft Security roles group or specific security groups.

keyFacts.fact: Copilot owner and Copilot contributor aren't Entra roles; they control only Security Copilot platform capabilities and give no access to security data by themselves.

Billing Administrator, Entra Compliance Administrator, Global Administrator, Intune Administrator and Security Administrator, plus some Purview roles, automatically inherit Copilot owner; Security Copilot enforces at least two owners.
Only owners can manage capacity, view the usage dashboard, change preinstalled plugin availability, and update data sharing options; contributors can create sessions and run/share promptbooks.
Plugins use on-behalf-of authentication, so an analyst with Copilot contributor still needs, for example, Microsoft Sentinel Reader to see Sentinel incidents through Copilot.
Use the Recommended Microsoft Security roles group (default) instead of Everyone; if Everyone is assigned, remove it first.
For MSSPs, GDAP is recommended and uses the customer's capacity; Azure Lighthouse uses the partner tenant's capacity.

steps: In Microsoft Entra admin center create security group SG-Copilot-Analysts and add Analyst1.

If Everyone is listed under Copilot contributor, remove it.
Select Add members, choose SG-Copilot-Analysts, role Copilot contributor, then Add.
Assign Analyst1 Microsoft Sentinel Reader on the Sentinel resource group so the Sentinel plugin returns data.

objectives.summary: Plugins give Security Copilot tools to reach data and services. Categories are Microsoft, non-Microsoft, websites and custom. Owners control whether contributors can add custom plugins for themselves or for everyone in the workspace, and can restrict preinstalled plugins to owners only. Custom plugins are YAML/JSON manifests (Descriptor and SkillGroups) using formats such as API (OpenAPI 3.0/3.0.1), KQL, GPT, or an OpenAI plugin link.

keyFacts.fact: Plugin sources are grouped as Microsoft, Non-Microsoft, Websites and Custom; users toggle plugins on or off in the Sources pane.
By default only owners can add custom plugins; owners can allow 'Owners and Contributors' for user scope and separately for organization/workspace scope.
Restricting a preinstalled plugin to Owners only takes effect immediately and affects embedded experiences too; new preinstalled plugins then default to owners only.
Plugins such as Microsoft Sentinel need per-user setup (gear/Set up), for example to choose a default workspace.
A custom plugin manifest has two required top-level keys, Descriptor and SkillGroups; API plugins support OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.0.1.
Products that integrate as plugins (such as non-Microsoft services) must be purchased separately.

objectives.portalPath: Security Copilot portal > prompt bar > Sources icon > Manage plugins; Home menu > Owner settings > Plugin settings

lab.title: Allow contributors to add personal custom plugins and upload a KQL plugin
steps: As an owner, open Owner settings > Plugin settings and set 'Who can add and manage their own custom plugins' to Owners and Contributors.

Create a YAML file with Descriptor (Name, DisplayName, Description, Settings for TenantId, WorkspaceName, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroupName) and a SkillGroups entry with Format: KQL, Target: Sentinel and a simple query such as SecurityIncident | take 10.
Select the Sources icon > Custom > Upload plugin, choose 'Just me', Security Copilot plugin, upload the file.
Complete the plugin setup values, then turn on the plugin toggle.
lab.verify: The plugin appears in the Custom section with a private tag and its skill can be invoked from the prompt bar.

objectives.summary: Security Copilot agents automate tasks such as phishing triage, threat intelligence briefings and Conditional Access optimization. You discover them in the Agents library or the Microsoft Security Store, set them up with an identity (a dedicated Microsoft Entra Agent ID is recommended), trigger and permissions, and then run, pause, edit and tune them through feedback and memory. Partner agents are bought in Security Store; agents that access Microsoft product data need Global Administrator approval. The agent and Security Store Learn pages carry a prerelease notice, and expanding the Phishing Triage Agent to other alert types is in preview.

keyFacts.fact: Agent setup lets you create an agent identity (Microsoft Entra Agent ID, currently Microsoft-built agents only) or connect an existing user account; creating an agent identity is recommended.

A partner-built agent that accesses Microsoft product data (for example Intune, Entra, Sentinel, Defender) requires a Global Administrator to approve its permissions before owners/contributors finish setup.
Security Store purchases are separate from Security Copilot: removing an agent doesn't end its subscription, and running agents consumes SCUs billed independently.
Getting an agent from Security Store needs Contributor or Owner on the Azure billing subscription and a Security Copilot owner or contributor role to set it up.

The Phishing Triage Agent needs Security Copilot capacity, Defender for Office 365 Plan 2, URBAC activated for Defender for Office 365, and the 'Email reported by user as malware or phish' alert policy; it auto-activates its plugins.
Feedback given to an agent is stored in its memory; owners/contributors can review it via Manage memory and reject feedback.

objectives.portalPath: Security Copilot portal > Agents (Set up); Home menu > Security Store; or Microsoft Entra admin center > Security Store

lab.title: Set up a Microsoft-built agent with an Agent ID
steps: Sign in to https://securitycopilot.microsoft.com and select Agents in the left navigation.
Choose a Microsoft-built agent available in your tenant (for example Threat Intelligence Briefing Agent) and select Set up.
Choose Create an agent identity, review required permissions, plugins and products, and set the trigger (scheduled or manual).
Complete setup, then select Run > One time.
After the run, give feedback to the agent and review it under ... > Manage memory.
lab.verify: The agent shows in Active agents / Agents in use with run history and output, and your feedback appears in Manage memory.
